q1: SELECT b1.name AS bar1, b2.name AS bar2 FROM bar AS b1, bar AS b2 WHERE NOT EXISTS(SELECT s1.beer FROM serves AS s1 WHERE s1.bar = b1.name AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM serves AS s2 WHERE s2.bar = b2.name AND s2.beer = s1.beer)) AND EXISTS(SELECT s2.beer FROM serves AS s2 WHERE s2.bar = b2.name AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM serves AS s1 WHERE s1.bar = b1.name AND s1.beer = s2.beer))
q2: SELECT DISTINCT s1.bar, s2.bar FROM serves AS s1, serves AS s2 WHERE s1.bar <> s2.bar AND EXISTS(SELECT * FROM serves AS s3 WHERE s3.beer IN (SELECT s3.beer FROM serves AS s4 WHERE s4.bar <> s3.bar AND NOT s4.beer IN (SELECT s5.beer FROM serves AS s5 WHERE s5.bar = s3.bar)))

explanation: Q1 and Q2 are not semantically equivalent because they are checking for different conditions related to the beers served by bars. Q1 is looking for bars that serve beers which no other bar serves, and Q2 is looking for pairs of bars where one bar serves a beer that the other does not, and vice versa.
